mechanisms.name: Cursor Local SDK Agent Execution

contract.input: Prompt string, optional tool definitions, system instructions, and configuration options
contract.output: Streamed message chunks, tool calls, finished status, and final response text
contract.lifecycle: Agent instance lifecycle: created -> active prompt -> tool execution -> completed -> idle

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: In-process or SQLite session storage identified by unique string session ID
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Full access to local custom tools, workspace files, and local shell commands subject to permissions
known_limitations: Requires local Node.js runtime
Local context bound by machine RAM and token budget

mechanisms.name: Cursor Cloud Agent Dispatch

contract.input: Repository URI, commit hash, goal description, and environment secrets
contract.output: Remote execution run ID, streamed telemetry logs, and final git branch/PR URI
contract.lifecycle: Queued -> Provisioning remote VM -> Cloning -> Executing -> Generating PR -> Finished

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Cursor Cloud persistent run storage with cryptographic run ID
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Cloud sandbox isolated containers with internet access and configured secrets
known_limitations: Network roundtrip latency
Requires active Cursor cloud subscription

mechanisms.name: Cursor Conversation Resume & Persistence
mechanisms.source_evidence: @cursor/sdk npm package: Agent.resume, Agent.list, SDK store

contract.input: Session ID string and optional resumed prompt
contract.output: Restored agent state with complete prior message history and active context
contract.lifecycle: Lookup stored session -> Rehydrate message state -> Re-attach custom tools -> Ready

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Persisted to disk SQLite / JSON conversation store keyed by session UUID
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Inherits original session tool definitions and authorization bounds
known_limitations: State rehydration fails if backing database or files are corrupted or deleted

mechanisms.name: Cursor Local Subagent Hierarchy
mechanisms.source_evidence: @cursor/sdk npm package: Agent.createChild, DAG task runner pattern

contract.input: Child role name, specialized system prompt, scoped tool whitelist, and parent context slice
contract.output: Structured child task result, telemetry metrics, and parent notification message
contract.lifecycle: Parent spawns child -> Child runs independently -> Emits result -> Parent collects -> Teardown

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Child session linked hierarchically to parent conversation ID
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Strict subset of parent permissions; cannot elevate privileges
known_limitations: Deep subagent recursion may exhaust process memory or file descriptors

mechanisms.name: Cursor In-Process TypeScript Custom Tools

contract.input: JSON schema parameters matching registered tool signature
contract.output: Arbitrary JSON-serializable output object or string returned to model
contract.lifecycle: Registered at startup -> Invoked during agent reasoning loop -> Synchronous/async execution -> Return

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Stateless tool handlers bound to host process lifecycle
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Can interact with local filesystem, network, and system APIs directly in Node.js
known_limitations: Tool execution blocks agent loop if asynchronous operations fail to timeout

mechanisms.name: Cursor Plugin Skill Format

contract.input: Slash command invocation (/command <args>) from user or parent agent
contract.output: Structured Markdown instructions, prompt expansion, and recommended tool calls
contract.lifecycle: Discovered from skills/ directory -> Matched on slash invocation -> Injected into prompt

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: File-based markdown skill definitions discovered at plugin registration time
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Inherits caller environment tool and permission boundaries
known_limitations: Static instruction format; dynamic logic requires host script or tool execution

mechanisms.name: Cursor Plugin Agent Persona Format
mechanisms.source_evidence: cursor/plugins repository: agents/<agent>.md persona and tool scoping definitions

contract.input: Target task description and agent invocation tag
contract.output: Specialized agent execution under defined persona and restricted toolset
contract.lifecycle: Loaded from agents/ -> Spawned as dedicated subagent or primary personality -> Completed

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: File-based markdown persona definitions with frontmatter role and capabilities
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Tools explicitly scoped in frontmatter tools whitelist
known_limitations: Model selection depends on host support and configured API keys

mechanisms.name: Cursor Persistent Context Rules (AGENTS.md & .cursor/rules)

contract.input: Workspace file pattern match or root directory context loading
contract.output: Persistent prompt constraints injected into every turn of every agent
contract.lifecycle: Evaluated at each user turn based on glob pattern matches or global root inclusion

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Committed repository files under .cursor/rules/ or root AGENTS.md
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Context injection only; no direct execution privileges
known_limitations: Consumes token context window on every turn

mechanisms.name: Cursor Lifecycle Hooks
mechanisms.source_evidence: cursor/cookbook: cookbook hooks examples and hooks/hooks.json definitions

contract.input: Event payload (session start, pre-tool, post-tool, stop) serialized as JSON
contract.output: Exit code 0 to permit action, non-zero to block, or modified tool arguments
contract.lifecycle: Event fires -> Hook script spawned -> Stdin JSON passed -> Stdout parsed -> Proceed or abort

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Configured in hooks/hooks.json or plugin manifest
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Executes as external script with host user privileges
known_limitations: Hook timeouts must be strictly enforced to avoid hanging the interactive UI

mechanisms.name: Cursor Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration
mechanisms.source_evidence: .mcp.json repository configuration and cursor-sdk plugin MCP integration

contract.input: JSON-RPC 2.0 requests over stdio or SSE transport
contract.output: Structured tool schema definitions, tool execution responses, and resource payloads
contract.lifecycle: Host starts MCP server process -> Handshake -> Tool discovery -> Model calls -> Server responds

mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Server controls exposed tools; host user approves initial server activation
known_limitations: Stdio transport requires local binary installed; SSE requires reachable server

mechanisms.name: Cursor Permissions & Local Auto-Review Engine
mechanisms.source_evidence: @cursor/sdk npm package: local.autoReview API and permissions.json

contract.input: Proposed tool invocation, command line string, target file path, and risk level
contract.output: Approval decision: allow, deny, or escalate to interactive human confirmation modal
contract.lifecycle: Tool call intercepted -> autoReview evaluated against rules -> Policy enforced

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Configured via policy files or programmable handler function
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Authoritative gatekeeper preventing unauthorized shell or filesystem writes
known_limitations: Cannot prevent side effects of pre-approved commands

mechanisms.name: Cursor Host CLI Interface
mechanisms.source_evidence: cursor / cursor-agent binary CLI help and omcu_capabilities.lock.json

contract.input: CLI arguments: --mode plan|ask, --print, --output-format json|stream-json, create-chat, ls, --resume
contract.output: Standard output JSON streams, session metadata, or interactive terminal session
contract.lifecycle: Invoked by user or script -> Runs agent loop -> Flushes output -> Exits with code

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Interacts with host local session database
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Runs with user terminal privileges and environment variables
known_limitations: Interactive terminal mode cannot be easily scripted without headless flags

mechanisms.name: Cursor Multi-Agent Window & Tabs
mechanisms.source_evidence: Cursor IDE native Multi-Chat and Agent Window architecture

contract.input: User message or agent invocation in dedicated chat tab
contract.output: Rendered conversational stream with integrated diff viewers and file link badges
contract.lifecycle: Tab opened -> Agent assigned -> Concurrent turns executed -> Tab closed/archived

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: GUI state backed by IDE workspace storage
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Access to IDE editor buffers, active selections, and terminal panes
known_limitations: GUI surface requires running Cursor desktop application

mechanisms.name: Cursor Git Worktree Workspace Isolation
mechanisms.source_evidence: cursor-team-kit and cookbook worktree execution patterns

contract.input: Branch name and target checkout directory
contract.output: Isolated filesystem working tree sharing underlying .git repository objects
contract.lifecycle: git worktree add -> Agent operates in worktree -> Branch committed -> Merged or pruned

mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Full filesystem access within the worktree boundary
known_limitations: Requires clean git repository state; simultaneous writes to same file handled via git branches

mechanisms.name: Cursor Background Automations
mechanisms.source_evidence: Cursor docs: background automations, scheduled runs, and event triggers

contract.input: Cron trigger or webhook event + workflow automation specification
contract.output: Autonomous headless agent execution run and pull request / notification output
contract.lifecycle: Scheduled event triggers -> Cloud runner spins up -> Executes task -> Emits report

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Cursor Cloud automation dashboard and run histories
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Scoped repository token permissions and cloud sandbox resources
known_limitations: Requires enterprise cloud configuration

mechanisms.name: Cursor Canvas & Artifact Interface
mechanisms.source_evidence: Cursor IDE Canvas interactive preview and artifact visualization panels

contract.input: Markdown, HTML, SVG, or JSON artifact payload
contract.output: Interactive side-by-side rendered visual canvas with live feedback controls
contract.lifecycle: Agent writes artifact -> Canvas panel renders -> User reviews / interacts -> Agent updates

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Stored in workspace scratch directory or embedded in conversation transcript
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Read-only display for user interaction; can dispatch actions to agent
known_limitations: Complex JS execution in canvas requires trusted sandbox mode

mechanisms.name: Cursor Adaptive Model Router
mechanisms.source_evidence: Cursor model selection settings: auto/fast/smart/reasoning dynamic routing

contract.input: Prompt complexity, active task type (code edit vs reasoning vs chat), and latency target
contract.output: Optimally routed LLM model endpoint invocation (Sonnet, Opus, GPT-5, Flash, etc.)
contract.lifecycle: Prompt classified at gateway -> Route selected -> Model invoked -> Tokens streamed

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Stateless model routing proxy managed by Cursor infrastructure
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Model capabilities aligned with selected backend
known_limitations: Automatic routing decisions may vary based on model provider availability

mechanisms.name: Cursor Plugin Command Format
mechanisms.source_evidence: cursor/plugins repository: commands/*.md standard command declarations

contract.input: User slash command (/command-name) invocation in chat prompt
contract.output: Expanded prompt instructions, workflow triggers, and command context
contract.lifecycle: Loaded from commands/ -> Matched on slash input -> Prompt expanded -> Executed

mechanisms.persistence_and_identity: Static markdown command definitions committed to commands/ directory
mechanisms.permissions_and_tools: Inherits caller environment tool and permission boundaries
known_limitations: Static markdown template without dynamic interactive input prompting
